name: Multi-gym chest press
form_cues: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest.
Press forward smoothly until arms are nearly straight.
Control the weight back until you feel a chest stretch.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up to the ears.
Letting the stack slam between reps.
safety: Adjust the seat before loading; keep the weight stack clear of hands and feet.
notes: Most home multi-gyms use a pulley-driven press arm; resistance may feel lighter than a commercial machine.

name: Multi-gym pec fly
form_cues: Keep a soft bend in the elbows throughout.
Squeeze the pads or handles together in front of your chest.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch, not a strain.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the hands instead of hugging with the arms.
Letting the arms travel too far back.
safety: Avoid overstretching the shoulders at the open position.

name: Multi-gym leg extension
form_cues: Line your knee up with the machine's pivot point.
Kick up until legs are straight and squeeze the quads.
Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
common_mistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum.
safety: Start light if you have knee pain and stop if it sharpens.
notes: Usually shares a station with the multi-gym leg curl.

name: Multi-gym leg curl
form_cues: Set the pad just above your heels.
Curl the pad towards your glutes without lifting your hips.
Return slowly to almost straight legs.
common_mistakes: Hips popping up off the bench.
Cutting the range short at the bottom.
safety: Keep your hips pressed down to protect the lower back.
notes: Depending on the model this is done seated, standing or lying on the leg-extension attachment.

name: Preacher curl
form_cues: Set the pad so your armpits sit snug on top.
Curl up without letting your elbows leave the pad.
Lower under control to almost straight arms.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast to the bottom and bouncing.
Lifting elbows or shoulders off the pad.
safety: Don't fully lock out under heavy load at the bottom; the biceps tendon is most stretched there.
notes: A straight barbell also works if you have no EZ bar.

name: Dumbbell preacher curl
form_cues: Rest the back of your upper arm flat on the pad.
Curl up, turning the pinkie slightly up at the top.
Lower slowly until the arm is nearly straight.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulder forward to finish the rep.
Going too heavy and losing the bottom half.
safety: Use a weight you can control at full stretch.
notes: Often done on the steep (vertical) side of the pad for a harder peak contraction.

name: Preacher hammer curl
form_cues: Hold the dumbbell with thumb up throughout.
Keep the elbow pinned to the pad as you curl.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Keep the wrist straight and neutral.
notes: Builds arm thickness and elbow-flexor strength.

name: Reverse-grip preacher curl
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down, hands shoulder-width.
Curl up while keeping wrists straight.
Lower with control; don't let the bar drop.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight for the grip.
safety: Go lighter than a regular preacher curl; forearms tire fast.
notes: Great for forearm and elbow health in pulling athletes.

name: Seated chest press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles are level with mid-chest.
Keep shoulder blades back and down against the pad.
Press out, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.
common_mistakes: Seat set too low or high.
Elbows flaring straight out to the sides.
safety: Set the seat height before loading, and keep wrists stacked over elbows.
notes: A safe way to train chest to failure without a spotter.

name: Iso-lateral chest press
form_cues: Load both sides evenly and set handles at mid-chest.
Drive the arms forward along their curved path together.
Lower slowly to a deep chest stretch.
common_mistakes: One arm doing more of the work.
safety: Make sure the arms are both on their stops before you load or unload plates.
notes: Independent arms help fix left-right imbalances.

name: Wide chest press machine
form_cues: Grip the wide handles with elbows slightly below shoulders.
Press forward and in, squeezing the chest.
Return slowly to a full stretch across the chest.
common_mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward at the top.
safety: Avoid an aggressive stretch if your shoulders are sensitive.
notes: The wider path puts more emphasis on the outer chest stretch than a standard chest press.

name: Single-arm machine chest press
form_cues: Brace your free hand on the seat or your hip.
Press one handle forward without twisting your torso.
Lower slowly and keep the shoulder blade pinned.
common_mistakes: Rotating the body to finish the rep.
safety: Keep the torso square to stop the lower back twisting.
notes: Best on machines with independent arms.

name: Lying chest press machine
form_cues: Lie with handles in line with your mid-chest.
Keep feet flat and upper back tight on the pad.
Press up, then lower slowly to a stretch.
safety: Make sure the starting position is safe before unracking.
notes: Mimics the bench press with no need for a spotter.

name: Incline press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start at upper chest.
Press up and slightly in, keeping shoulders down.
Lower slowly until hands are level with the chest.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, turning it into a shoulder press.
safety: Keep shoulder blades back to protect the front of the shoulder.

name: Iso-lateral incline press
form_cues: Set the seat so handles sit at upper-chest level.
Drive both arms up evenly.
Lower under control to a deep upper-chest stretch.
safety: Rack both arms before getting up or changing plates.
notes: Arms can be pressed one at a time for unilateral work.

name: Decline chest press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start at lower chest.
Press down and forward until arms are nearly straight.
Return slowly and keep the chest proud.
safety: Use the foot lever or a partner to get into position if the start is deep.
notes: Nearest app gear id is the seated chest press machine.

name: Iso-lateral decline press
form_cues: Load both sides evenly before sitting down.
Press down and out along the arc together.
Lower with control to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Pushing with one side more than the other.
safety: Make sure both arms are resting on their stops before loading.

name: Pec deck fly
form_cues: Set the seat so handles are at chest height.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and hug the handles together.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch, then squeeze back.
common_mistakes: Letting the arms travel far behind the body.
Pressing with the hands instead of moving at the shoulder.
safety: Limit the backward stretch if you have shoulder pain.
notes: Pause one second at the squeeze for more chest work.

name: Single-arm pec deck fly
form_cues: Sit side-on or square and hold the frame with your free hand.
Sweep one handle across your body past midline.
Return slowly to a controlled stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to move the weight.
Using too much load to cross midline.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and back throughout.
notes: Crossing past midline gives a stronger peak contraction than two-arm flies.

name: Assisted dip
form_cues: Kneel or stand on the pad and grip the dip handles.
Lower until upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up, leaning slightly forward for chest.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulders.
safety: More counterweight makes it easier; stop short of any shoulder pinch.
notes: Reduce the assistance over time as you get stronger.

name: Seated dip machine
form_cues: Sit tall with your back on the pad and grip the handles.
Press down until arms are straight, elbows close to sides.
Let the handles rise slowly to about 90 degrees.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward and pushing with shoulders.
safety: Don't let the handles rise so high that your shoulders roll forward.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the tricep extension machine.

name: Assisted pull-up
form_cues: Grip just outside shoulder width, palms forward.
Pull your chest towards the bar, elbows down to your ribs.
Lower slowly to fully straight arms.
common_mistakes: Half reps that skip the bottom stretch.
safety: Step on and off the pad carefully; more counterweight means more help.
notes: Cut the assistance by one plate when you can do 3 x 10.

name: Assisted chin-up
form_cues: Grip shoulder-width with palms facing you.
Drive elbows down and bring chin over the bar.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Craning the neck to reach the bar.
Dropping fast on the way down.
safety: Keep the shoulders active at the bottom rather than hanging loose.
notes: Biceps help more here, so most people find it easier than the pull-up.

name: Chest-supported row machine
form_cues: Set the chest pad so you can just reach the handles.
Pull elbows back and squeeze shoulder blades together.
Let the arms straighten slowly and the shoulders reach forward.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad.
safety: Chest support takes load off the lower back.
notes: Neutral grip hits lats more; wide overhand hits upper back more.

name: Iso-lateral row
form_cues: Keep your chest on the pad and feet planted.
Row the handles back towards your hips.
Reach forward fully on the way back for a lat stretch.
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight with the torso.
safety: Load both sides evenly before starting.
notes: Arms can be worked one at a time.

name: Iso-lateral high row
form_cues: Secure your thighs under the pads.
Pull the handles down and back towards your lower chest.
Return slowly with a full stretch overhead.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the hands rather than driving elbows.
safety: Keep the chest up and avoid jerky reps.
notes: Sits between a pulldown and a row; great for lat width. App gear id is the nearest match.

name: Iso-lateral low row
form_cues: Sit with chest on the pad and grab the low handles.
Row elbows back past your torso towards your hips.
Reach forward slowly for a full lat stretch.
safety: Keep your chest on the pad the whole time.
notes: The low-to-high path biases the lower lats.

name: Wide-grip machine row
form_cues: Grip the wide handles with palms facing down.
Pull elbows out and back to shoulder height.
Squeeze shoulder blades, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the belly instead of the chest.
safety: Keep the neck relaxed and chin tucked.
notes: Targets the upper back more than the lats.

name: Iso-lateral D.Y. row
form_cues: Set the chest pad so you reach the handles with straight arms.
Pull with an underhand or neutral grip towards your waist.
Lower under control for a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Using the legs to drive the weight.
safety: Keep the chest supported to protect the lower back.
notes: Mimics the underhand barbell row made popular by Dorian Yates.

name: T-bar row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, knees soft.
Row the handles towards your upper stomach.
Lower slowly without losing your back position.
common_mistakes: Standing up taller with each rep to cheat.
safety: Keep a neutral spine; skip this if you have lower-back pain and use the chest-supported version.
notes: A landmine with a V-handle works if your gym has no T-bar station.

name: Chest-supported T-bar row
form_cues: Lie chest-down on the pad with feet on the platform.
Row the handles up until elbows pass your torso.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad.
Jerking the first part of the rep.
safety: Step on the platform carefully and keep your chin neutral.
notes: Easier on the lower back than the standing T-bar row.

name: Iso-lateral front lat pulldown
form_cues: Lock your thighs under the pads.
Pull the handles down towards your shoulders, elbows to ribs.
Let the arms rise slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Leaning back a lot to cheat.
safety: Control the return so the plates don't yank your shoulders.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lat pulldown machine.

name: Pullover machine
form_cues: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the pivot.
Drive the elbows down in an arc to your stomach.
Return slowly to a deep overhead stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the hands instead of the elbows.
Arching the lower back at the top.
safety: Limit the top stretch if overhead positions hurt your shoulders.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lat pulldown machine. Trains lats without the biceps tiring first.

name: Machine rear delt row
form_cues: Use a wide overhand grip and set your chest on the pad.
Row with elbows flared out to shoulder level.
Squeeze the back of the shoulders, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a regular row with elbows in.
safety: Keep it light and controlled; the rear delts are small.

name: Back extension
form_cues: Set the pad just below your hip bones.
Hinge down with a flat back, then rise until body is straight.
Squeeze glutes at the top without over-arching.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending past straight at the top.
safety: Don't arch past a straight line; stop if you feel sharp back pain.
notes: Hold a plate to your chest to add load.

name: Glute-focused back extension
form_cues: Turn feet out and keep chin tucked, upper back slightly rounded.
Lower by hinging at the hips.
Drive hips into the pad by squeezing the glutes.
common_mistakes: Using the lower back to lift.
Setting the pad too high so you can't hinge.
safety: Keep the movement at the hips, not the lower back.
notes: Setting the pad lower on the thighs lets the hips move more.

name: Single-leg back extension
form_cues: Hook one foot under the roller, other leg free.
Hinge down slowly with hips square.
Rise by driving the working hip into the pad.
safety: Go slowly; the single leg makes balance harder.

name: GHD back extension
form_cues: Set the pad at your hips with feet locked under the rollers.
Lower your torso towards the floor with a flat back.
Rise until your body is horizontal, not higher.
safety: Lift no higher than straight; this horizontal version is harder than 45 degrees.

name: Glute-ham raise
form_cues: Lock feet in with knees just behind the pad.
Start upright, then lower forward with a straight line hips to head.
Pull yourself back up by digging toes into the plate.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to cheat.
Dropping uncontrolled on the way down.
safety: Build up slowly; push off a box or use a band if you can't control the lowering.
notes: One of the best hamstring builders for knee flexion and hip extension together.

name: GHD hip extension
form_cues: Set the pad so your hips hang just off the front.
Hinge down from the hips, keeping the spine neutral.
Squeeze glutes to bring your body back to straight.
safety: Keep the motion at the hips; stop if the lower back takes over.

name: Reverse hyper
form_cues: Lie chest-down with hips at the pad's edge and grip the handles.
Swing legs up until in line with the body, squeezing glutes.
Lower under control; don't let the pendulum yank you.
safety: Start light; the strap and pendulum can whip the spine if you go too heavy.
notes: Popular as a lower-back rehab and strength accessory.

name: Seated back extension machine
form_cues: Sit with the pad across your upper back and feet secure.
Push back slowly until your torso is upright or slightly past.
Return to the start with control.
safety: Use a light load and slow reps; skip if it aggravates back pain.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the Roman chair.

name: Machine shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight holding the handles.
Lift shoulders straight up towards the ears.
Pause, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Keep the neck neutral; don't jut your chin forward.

name: Machine upright row
form_cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Lead with the elbows up to about shoulder height.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
safety: Stop at shoulder height and skip it if you feel a pinch.

name: Seated shoulder press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start just above shoulder level.
Press up without locking out hard.
Lower slowly until hands are near the shoulders.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad.
Seat too high so the range is short.
safety: Keep the back flat on the pad.

name: Iso-lateral shoulder press
form_cues: Load both sides evenly and sit tall.
Press both handles overhead along their arc.
Lower slowly to shoulder height.
safety: Rack both arms before standing up.
notes: Press one arm at a time to even out imbalances.

name: Lateral raise machine
form_cues: Line your shoulders up with the machine's pivot.
Raise the arms out to shoulder height, leading with the elbows.
Lower slowly without letting the stack rest.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the weight up with traps.
safety: Stop at shoulder height if raising higher pinches.
notes: Keeps constant tension through the whole range.

name: Single-arm machine lateral raise
form_cues: Sit tall and work one arm at a time.
Raise the elbow out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly and keep the shoulder down.
safety: Keep the weight modest and the shoulder relaxed.

name: Rear delt machine
form_cues: Face the pad with handles at shoulder height.
Sweep arms back in a wide arc, slight bend in elbows.
Return slowly without letting the stack touch.
common_mistakes: Squeezing shoulder blades so traps take over.
safety: Use moderate weight; the rear delts are small.
notes: Most pec decks double as a rear delt machine with the handles reversed.

name: Single-arm reverse pec deck
form_cues: Sit side-on or square and grip the opposite handle.
Sweep the arm back across your body to shoulder line.
Return slowly to the start.
common_mistakes: Pulling past the line of the body.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and the movement smooth.
notes: Reaching across the body gives a longer range than the two-arm version.

name: Bicep curl machine
form_cues: Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot.
Curl up and squeeze the biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until arms are nearly straight.
safety: Don't let the weight drop at the bottom.

name: Single-arm machine curl
form_cues: Work one arm at a time with the elbow on the pad.
Curl up fully and squeeze.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Keep the wrist straight.
notes: Best on machines with independent handles.

name: Tricep extension machine
form_cues: Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot.
Push the handles down until arms are straight.
Return slowly without letting elbows lift off the pad.
safety: Keep the elbows fixed on the pad.

name: Overhead triceps extension machine
form_cues: Sit with elbows pointing up and resting on the pad.
Extend the arms until straight overhead.
Lower slowly to a deep triceps stretch.
safety: Limit the stretch if the elbows or shoulders feel irritated.
notes: Overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps.

name: Leg press
form_cues: Place feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.
Lower until knees reach about 90 degrees, hips stay down.
Press through the whole foot without locking the knees.
common_mistakes: Lower back peeling off the pad at the bottom.
safety: Never lock out hard, and keep the safety handles in reach.

name: Seated leg press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so knees start at about 90 degrees.
Push through mid-foot until legs are nearly straight.
Return slowly without letting the stack slam.
common_mistakes: Seat too close so the hips round.
safety: Keep the lower back on the pad.
notes: A gentle starting point for beginners.

name: Single-leg leg press
form_cues: Place one foot in the middle of the platform.
Lower slowly, keeping the knee in line with the toes.
Press up without locking out.
safety: Use much lighter weight than two-leg pressing.
notes: Great for spotting and fixing side-to-side differences.

name: Wide-stance leg press
form_cues: Place feet wide with toes turned out slightly.
Lower with knees tracking over the toes.
Drive through the heels to press up.
safety: Only go as deep as your hips allow without rounding.

name: High-foot leg press
form_cues: Place feet high on the platform, hip-width.
Lower until hips are deeply flexed but still on the pad.
Push through the heels to the top.
safety: Stop the descent before your lower back rounds.
notes: Moving feet higher shifts work from quads to glutes and hamstrings.

name: Narrow-stance leg press
form_cues: Place feet hip-width or closer, low on the platform.
Lower slowly, letting knees travel forward.
Press up through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Going so deep the lower back rounds.
safety: Skip low foot placement if it bothers your knees.

name: Vertical leg press
form_cues: Lie flat with hips directly under the platform.
Unlock and lower the platform towards your chest.
Press straight up without locking the knees.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the floor pad.
safety: Always use the safety stops; this machine loads straight down onto you.

name: Leg press calf raise
form_cues: Place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Keep knees soft and press through the toes.
Lower heels slowly for a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to move the weight.
safety: Keep the safety handles locked; feet can slip off the edge.

name: Hack squat
form_cues: Set shoulders under the pads and feet shoulder-width.
Lower until thighs are at least parallel, back flat.
Drive up through mid-foot without locking out.
common_mistakes: Hips sliding off the back pad.
safety: Engage the safety catches before you start.

name: Reverse hack squat
form_cues: Face the back pad with chest on it and shoulders under the pads.
Sit hips back and down, keeping chest on the pad.
Drive up through the heels.
safety: Use the safety stops and start light.
notes: More hip hinge than the regular hack squat, so the glutes work harder.

name: Pendulum squat
form_cues: Set shoulders under the pads with feet forward on the platform.
Sink deep with the arc, knees travelling forward.
Drive back up without locking out.
common_mistakes: Feet set too far back so heels lift.
safety: Use the safety lock; depth is deep, so build up gradually.
notes: Very quad-dominant with little load on the spine.

name: Belt squat
form_cues: Attach the belt low around your hips and stand tall.
Squat down keeping torso upright.
Drive up through mid-foot.
common_mistakes: Belt riding up onto the lower back.
safety: Great option when the spine needs a break; unhook the belt only when the lever is racked.
notes: Loads the legs without compressing the spine.

name: Belt squat march
form_cues: Stand tall with the belt loaded and knees soft.
March in place, lifting knees to hip height.
Keep hips level and steady.
common_mistakes: Shuffling feet instead of driving knees.
safety: Keep the load moderate and stop if form breaks.
notes: A conditioning and hip-stability finisher.

name: V-squat
form_cues: Stand on the platform with shoulders under the pads.
Squat down with a slight lean following the machine's arc.
Press up through the whole foot.
safety: Use the safety catches.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the hack squat machine.

name: Leg extension
form_cues: Line your knee up with the pivot and set the pad on your lower shins.
Extend fully and squeeze the quads.
Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
safety: Use moderate loads if you have knee pain.

name: Single-leg leg extension
form_cues: Work one leg at a time with the other relaxed.
Extend fully and pause.
Lower slowly.
safety: Go lighter than half your two-leg weight to start.

name: Lying leg curl
form_cues: Lie face down with knees just off the pad's edge.
Curl heels towards your glutes, hips pressed down.
Lower slowly until legs are almost straight.
safety: Keep the hips down to protect the lower back.

name: Single-leg lying leg curl
form_cues: Work one leg at a time with hips square.
Curl the heel up fully.
Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Hip on the working side lifting.
safety: Start light; it's easy to strain a hamstring with jerky reps.

name: Seated leg curl
form_cues: Lock the thigh pad down firmly.
Curl the heels down and back as far as you can.
Return slowly to almost straight legs.
safety: Lean forward slightly for more hamstring stretch.
notes: The seated position stretches the hamstrings more than lying.

name: Single-leg seated leg curl
form_cues: Lock the thigh pad down and work one leg.
Curl the heel back fully.
Return slowly.
safety: Keep the pad tight on the thighs.

name: Standing leg curl
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad behind your ankle.
Curl the heel up towards your glute.
Lower slowly without swinging.
safety: Hold the handles and keep the hips square.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lying leg curl machine.

name: Kneeling leg curl
form_cues: Kneel with forearms on the pads and heel under the roller.
Curl the heel up towards your glute.
Lower slowly.
safety: Keep the hips steady.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lying leg curl machine.

name: Standing calf raise
form_cues: Stand with balls of feet on the edge and shoulders under the pads.
Rise as high as you can and pause.
Lower slowly to a deep heel stretch.
safety: Pause at the bottom to avoid Achilles strain.

name: Single-leg calf raise machine
form_cues: Stand on one foot on the edge.
Rise high and pause at the top.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Keep a light grip on the handles for balance.

name: Seated calf raise
form_cues: Set the pad snug on your lower thighs.
Rise high onto the balls of your feet.
Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
safety: Release the safety lever only once the pad is set.
notes: Bent knees bias the soleus.

name: Single-leg seated calf raise
form_cues: Place one foot on the platform under the pad.
Rise as high as possible.
Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
safety: Keep the pad secure.

name: Donkey calf raise
form_cues: Hinge forward with hips under the pad and back flat.
Rise high on your toes.
Lower to a deep stretch.
safety: Keep the spine neutral.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the standing calf machine.

name: Hack squat calf raise
form_cues: Stand with balls of feet on the platform edge.
Rise high and pause.
Lower slowly.
safety: Watch foot placement on the edge.

name: Hip adduction machine
form_cues: Sit tall with pads on the inside of your knees.
Squeeze the legs together.
Open slowly to a comfortable stretch.
safety: Don't force a stretch past what's comfortable.

name: Hip abduction machine
form_cues: Sit tall with pads on the outside of your knees.
Push the legs apart.
Return slowly.
safety: Keep the movement smooth.

name: Leaning hip abduction
form_cues: Sit and lean forward from the hips, holding the frame.
Push the knees out.
Return slowly.
safety: Keep the back flat.
notes: Leaning forward shifts work towards the upper glute max.

name: Multi-hip abduction
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad on the outside of your thigh.
Lift the leg sideways.
Lower slowly.
safety: Hold the handles for balance.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the abductor machine.

name: Multi-hip glute extension
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad behind your thigh.
Drive the leg back.
Return slowly.
safety: Brace the core.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the glute kickback machine.

name: Hip thrust machine
form_cues: Set the belt across your hips and feet flat.
Drive hips up until body is straight.
Lower slowly.
safety: Tuck the chin and keep ribs down.

name: Single-leg hip thrust machine
form_cues: Set up as normal and lift one foot off.
Drive the hips up through the planted heel.
Lower slowly.
safety: Use much lighter load than two-leg.

name: Glute kickback machine
form_cues: Set the pad behind your knee or foot.
Drive the leg back and up.
Return slowly.
safety: Brace the core to protect the lower back.
